title: How Nokia Lost Its Empire
sources: TEST SCRIPT - fact-check before publishing anything real.

scenes.narration: In 2007, Nokia sold roughly half of all the smartphones on Earth.
scenes.subtitle: How an empire fell

scenes.narration: Its phones were in pockets from Helsinki to Jakarta.
scenes.query: busy city street crowd people walking

scenes.narration: It began in Finland, home to about five and a half million people.
Founded in 1865 as a paper mill, it reinvented itself again and again.
scenes.prompt: 19th century Finnish paper mill beside a river in winter, wooden buildings, smoke rising, dramatic light

scenes.narration: By the late nineties, it was the world's biggest phone maker.
At its peak, half of all smartphones sold carried its name.
Then, in 2007, Apple launched the iPhone.
scenes.query: hand using smartphone touchscreen close up

scenes.narration: Nokia's phones still sold, but its software could not keep up.
scenes.prompt: an old generic candybar mobile phone with a green screen on a dark table, moody low key light, shallow depth of field

scenes.narration: In 2011, its new chief executive told his staff the company had fallen behind.
scenes.quote: We have fallen behind, we have missed big trends, and we have lost time.
scenes.author: Stephen Elop, 2011

scenes.narration: In 2013, Microsoft bought the phone business for 5.4 billion euros.
This is how an empire lost its way.
